extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, investor relations (IR) teams, and communications staff at publicly traded companies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for crafting press releases aimed at the investment community—sharing financial results, strategic updates, and other shareholder-relevant news in a clear, compliant, and investor-focused way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Including key performance indicators (KPIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Including key performance indicators (KPIs) in your investor relations press releases is crucial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KPIs help align your company's performance with market expectations, build credibility, and facilitate comparisons with peers; include them to contribute to a strong strategic narrative and long-term investor confidence. No specific KPI list is mandated on the page, but include the metrics investors expect for your business/industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start With a Clear and Concise Headline
rubrics_metrics.description: Being direct is important when it comes to speaking to investors. They need to know if your release is good news or bad news for their investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep it short and concise, put important figures front and center (e.g., 'doubled sales across Q2'). Avoid hype or exaggeration. Ensure the headline matches the content of the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top the Piece With the Most Important Details
rubrics_metrics.description: Like with any news release, it’s crucial you lead with the important info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the company's story in simple English and provide a clear, compelling narrative explaining why the release is issued and what it means for investors. Do not bury bad news; investors should not need to dig through the release for key information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Financial Data and Performance Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Your key numbers should be really easy to understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sales growth, turnover figures, share values, market analysis, trends, year-over-year comparisons and other important elements an investor needs. Highlight main results (often bullet points at top). If anomalies exist (one-time events, unusual items), explain them to provide context and reassure investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes from Leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Include quotes from the leadership team to provide context when your press release contains good or bad news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short, focused quotes from the CEO, CFO, or top executives that align with company strategy and articulate context/future goals. For bad news, a leader should make a statement. If more information is needed, direct stakeholders to phone interviews or shareholder meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward-Looking Statements
rubrics_metrics.description: When wrapping up your release, it's a good idea to look to the future with forecasts or strategic direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include revenue or earnings forecasts or planned initiatives, but use cautious phrasing (e.g., 'we expect', 'we aim to') rather than firm promises. Add a brief legal disclaimer (safe harbor) about forward-looking information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure Regulatory Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sure that the press release follows all relevant regulations and required disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check SEC guidelines for public companies, include required disclosures and a safe harbor statement for forward-looking information, and double-check the accuracy of all publicly available data. Consult legal if unsure to avoid regulatory or litigation risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and Distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate timing and distribution carefully to ensure accuracy and avoid the appearance of burying news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with finance to ensure data is ready; file releases within regulatory timeframes; avoid issuing on major public holidays that suggest hiding bad news. Use newswire services (e.g., Cision PR Newswire, Bloomberg) for wide distribution and publish on the company website (investor section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Earnings Reports and Financial Results (content type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Earnings releases provide a snapshot of a company’s financial health over a period and are a crucial part of investor communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include revenue, net income, earnings per share (EPS), YoY comparisons, and factors that affected the results. Use bullet points to highlight main results for quick scanning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mergers, Acquisitions, and Partnerships (content type)
rubrics_metrics.description: When companies join forces or make major deals, investors need timely, clear information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain parties involved, financial terms, expected benefits, timeline if applicable, and how the deal fits the company's strategy. Consider quotes from leaders of both companies to show alignment and confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stock Splits, Buybacks, or Dividends (content type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Announcements that directly affect shareholder value and share structure require clear explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the nature of the change (split, buyback, dividend), reasons for it, and implications for investors (e.g., affordability, return). Provide context so investors understand how it signals company strategy or confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership Changes or Corporate Governance Updates (content type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investors expect prompt notice of leadership appointments, departures, or governance changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the new leader’s background and qualifications, short quotes about their role, and explanations of how governance changes align with shareholder interests. Explain policy/structural changes and any effects on investor rights or voting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Overly Technical Language
rubrics_metrics.description: Using too much jargon or complex terms can confuse readers; write in plain English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain tricky financial concepts simply; remember shareholder bases may have mixed financial backgrounds. Aim to communicate clearly rather than impress with technical language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and Inclusion of Relevant Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not hide or omit important information; missing details damage trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be upfront about positive and negative news. Include all relevant data points (revenue, profit margins, growth rates) and avoid cherry-picking only favorable numbers—highlight them but provide full context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and Readability (formatting guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A press release for investors should be concise, scannable, and well-structured for quick comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a compelling headline, dateline, and a lead paragraph that summarizes key points. Use bullet points to highlight financial data and make the release easy to scan. Finish with a 'throw forward'—projections, next steps, or announcement of next earnings call—to leave a forward-looking note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution Targets and Contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and reach out to the most relevant audiences and contacts when distributing IR releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include major shareholders, financial media outlets, investment analysts, wire services, industry-specific publications, and influential financial bloggers as part of distribution strategy. Provide clear media or investor contact info in the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the IR Team in Process and Follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: The IR department generally crafts content, ensures accuracy, and manages distribution and stakeholder follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with finance, legal, and executives for accuracy; handle distribution and follow-up with media and investors; track and report on the release's impact; field inquiries from media and investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Timing/Appearance Pitfalls (operational anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Poor timing or perceived concealment can undermine trust even if content is accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid issuing releases at times that imply you are 'burying' bad news (e.g., major public holidays). Ensure filings occur within regulatory windows so investors do not view timing as manipulative.
